items.title: install_and_import raises UnboundLocalError when pip/pip3 install fails
items.body:
## Background

`interpreter/terminal_interface/magic_commands.py::install_and_import(package)` tries `__import__(package)`, and on `ImportError` attempts to install it via pip (falling back to pip3). A `finally:` block registers the module in `globals()`.

## Problem

```python
def install_and_import(package):
    try:
        module = __import__(package)
    except ImportError:
        try:
            ...
            module = __import__(package)
        except subprocess.CalledProcessError:
            # If pip fails, try pip3
            try:
                subprocess.check_call([sys.executable, "-m", "pip3", "install", package], ...)
            except subprocess.CalledProcessError:
                print(f"Failed to install package {package}.")
                return
    finally:
        globals()[package] = module
    return module
```

When pip **and** pip3 both fail, the inner `except` returns before `module` is ever bound, so the `finally:` clause raises:

```
UnboundLocalError: cannot access local variable 'module' where it is not associated with a value
```

The same crash happens when pip fails but pip3 **succeeds**: `module` is still unbound after the pip3 branch (which never re-imports), so `finally` raises instead of returning the module. In both cases the intended behavior is a graceful print + `None`.

## Visible symptoms

- Full install failure: prints "Failed to install package X." then crashes with `UnboundLocalError` instead of returning `None`.
- pip3-fallback success: silently crashes with `UnboundLocalError` even though the install succeeded.

## What this PR should change

Initialize `module = None` before the `try`, and re-import after a successful pip3 install (`module = __import__(package)`), so the `finally` block is safe on all paths.

## Tests

- pip3-fallback path: `__import__` raises, pip `check_call` raises `CalledProcessError`, pip3 succeeds → returns the module.
- full-failure path: both installs raise → returns `None` (no `UnboundLocalError`).

items.title: `extract_corpus_parallel` misreports failed chunks as successful model omissions
items.body:
## Summary

When a semantic chunk raises before returning a model response, `extract_corpus_parallel()` correctly reports the chunk failure and increments `failed_chunks`, but the final reconciliation warning then describes the same file as if the model returned a successful response and omitted it.

Confirmed on v0.9.63 (`eaaec1abd99d3a7fb30301ccb49f4cc72ae34011`).

## Minimal reproduction

```python
import io
from contextlib import redirect_stderr
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
from unittest.mock import patch

from graphify.llm import extract_corpus_parallel

with TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    doc = Path(d) / "guide.md"
    doc.write_text("# Guide\n", encoding="utf-8")
    stderr = io.StringIO()
    with patch(
        "graphify.llm._extract_with_adaptive_retry",
        side_effect=ImportError(
            "OpenAI package not installed. pip install 'graphifyy[gemini]'."
        ),
    ), redirect_stderr(stderr):
        result = extract_corpus_parallel(
            [doc], backend="gemini", token_budget=None,
            chunk_size=1, max_concurrency=1,
        )
    print(stderr.getvalue())
    assert result["failed_chunks"] == 1
```

## Actual output

```text
[graphify] chunk 1/1 failed: OpenAI package not installed. pip install 'graphifyy[gemini]'.
[graphify] WARNING: 1/1 semantic chunk(s) failed — see errors above. Partial results returned.
[graphify] WARNING: 1/1 dispatched file(s) produced no nodes and are absent from the graph: guide.md. The model returned a response but omitted them; a re-run will retry them.
```

The final sentence contradicts the preceding failure: no model response existed.

## Cause

The dispatch/return reconciliation computes every dispatched file with no returned node as `uncovered`, but it does not retain which files belonged to chunks that raised. The single omission warning is therefore used for two distinct cases:

1. a chunk failed before returning a usable result; and
2. a chunk succeeded, but its response omitted one or more files.

## Expected

Files from failed chunks should be described as failed before returning a usable result. The existing “model returned a response but omitted them” wording should remain only for files absent from successful chunk results.

This matters for missing optional dependencies as well as provider/backend errors: the first error tells the operator what to install or fix, while the final warning currently sends them toward model-output debugging instead.

items.title: [Bug]: First-run (native Windows) install fails at the Python-dependencies stage — “INSTALL DIDN'T FINISH / dependency install failed”

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
## Bug Description

A fresh Hermes install on a Windows laptop does not complete. After the
standalone bootstrap installer (Hermes-Setup) runs its stages, it aborts and
shows the red failure screen:

> **INSTALL DIDN'T FINISH**
> dependency install failed
> [Retry install]  [Open logs]
> Log: `C:\Users\User\AppData\Local\hermes\logs\bootstrap-installer.log`

This is the first-run "install" flow (not the in-app updater): the window
title is "Hermes", the primary button is **Retry install**, and the log path
points at `bootstrap-installer.log` — i.e. the standalone Tauri bootstrap
installer in *install mode*.

Clicking **Retry install** re-runs the same stage and fails again (not
verified — no log captured yet).

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Fresh Windows laptop, no prior Hermes install.
2. Run the Hermes bootstrap installer (`Hermes-Setup.exe` / the first-run
   onboarding) in install mode.
3. Installer progresses through early stages, then fails at the Python
   dependencies stage.
4. Failure screen appears (see Bug Description). Exact stage boundary and
   underlying error are in `bootstrap-installer.log` — **not yet captured**.

> Needed to confirm: (a) the Hermes/installer version, (b) Windows version,
> (c) the full tail of `C:\Users\User\AppData\Local\hermes\logs\bootstrap-installer.log`
> around the failed `dependencies` stage. `hermes debug share` (or
> `--local`) would attach it.

## Expected Behavior

The `dependencies` stage installs the Python environment + hermes-agent
package successfully and the installer advances to the remaining stages
(node, desktop) and shows the "launch Hermes" success screen.

## Actual Behavior

The `dependencies` stage reports `ok=false`, the Rust bootstrap emits a
`failed` event, and the UI lands on the failure screen with the subtitle
"dependency install failed". Install is not complete.

## Affected Component

- Setup / Installation
- (bootstrap installer / desktop)

## Messaging Platform

- N/A (CLI only) — this is the installer, not a gateway.

## Operating System

Windows (laptop). Exact build not captured — see "Needed to confirm" above.

## Python Version

Not captured (install fails before a working venv exists; the installer is
supposed to provision it).

## Hermes Version

Not captured. Local reference checkout that reproduces the *screen* is
bootstrap-installer 0.21.1 / desktop 0.17.6 (commit 6289cd5c20, 2026-09-28).

## Debug Report

Not available from the reporter yet — the machine is a laptop and the
installer failed before a working `hermes` CLI existed to run
`hermes debug share`. Please attach the log file directly instead.

## Additional Logs / Traceback

Only the summary line is on screen. The failing stage's real stdout/stderr
is in `C:\Users\User\AppData\Local\hermes\logs\bootstrap-installer.log` and
must be captured to pin the exact failing command (likely a `uv sync --locked`
or `uv pip install` step, or the post-install baseline-import check).

## Root Cause Analysis

The subtitle shown ("dependency install failed") is **not** a hard-coded UI
string. On the failure screen
(`apps/bootstrap-installer/src/routes/failure.tsx`), the subtitle is
`bootstrap.error` (falling back to "Something went wrong during
installation."). `bootstrap.error` is set by the Rust backend when a stage
fails:

- `apps/bootstrap-installer/src-tauri/src/bootstrap.rs` — when a stage's JSON
  result frame has `ok=false`, it emits
  `BootstrapEvent::Failed { stage: Some(<name>), error: frame.reason }`
  (see the `Some(frame) => { ... }` arm, roughly lines 805–825). `frame.reason`
  is the PowerShell `$result.reason` from `scripts/install.ps1`
  `Invoke-Stage`'s `catch { $result.reason = "$_" }` (roughly lines 4979–4982).

So "dependency install failed" is the throw message from the **`dependencies`**
stage worker. In `scripts/install.ps1`:

- Stage definition: `@{ Name = "dependencies"; ... Worker = "Stage-Dependencies" }`
  (line ~4854) → `Stage-Dependencies { Resolve-UvCmd; Install-Dependencies }`
  (line ~4907).
- The throwing sites in `Install-Dependencies` (line 2967+) are:
  - `throw "Failed to install hermes-agent package even with no extras. Inspect the uv pip install output above."`
  - `throw "Install reported success but $venvPython does not exist. The dependency sync likely landed in a sibling .venv\ directory..."`
  - `throw "Baseline imports failed in $InstallDir\venv (dotenv/openai/rich/prompt_toolkit)..."`
  - plus a bare `throw` near the end of the function.

The exact string "dependency install failed" is not present in the current
`main` checkout of `install.ps1`'s dependency stage, which suggests the
reporter's build is a slightly different version — another reason the
**Hermes/installer version** matters. Two directions worth checking:

1. **A real dependency failure on this machine** (network/PyPI reachability,
   an existing partial `.venv`, a locked file from a prior Hermes process,
   or a UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT / sibling-`.venv` drift).
2. **A message/UX gap**: the failure screen shows a generic
   "dependency install failed" with no inline detail and no easy way to copy
   the log, so the actionable error is buried. Even if (1) is the root cause,
   (2) is worth hardening — surface the failing command + last stderr line
   on the failure screen and offer "Copy log".

## Proposed Fix

None offered from the reporter (reproduction + log still needed). If the
failure is environmental, the installer's existing venv-transaction/rollback
path should already cover it; the open question is whether it's doing so on
this machine.

## Are you willing to submit a PR?

- I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR (reporter is the fleet operator;
  can follow up with the log and a fix once the exact failing command is known).

---

---
_Reported from the fleet operator machine, via a logged-in GitHub browser session._

items.title: [Feature]: Installer resilience improvements for GitHub-restricted networks (mainland China) - stale script cache, no mirror fallback, misleading recovery hints

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
## Problem or Use Case

I just completed an install/upgrade of Hermes on a Chinese-locale Windows machine behind GitHub-restricted networking. The install only succeeded after manual intervention at **five** separate points; each one would silently fail or loop forever for a user who doesn't read the bootstrap log. Full failure chain:

**1. Stale cached bootstrap script → `INSTALL DIDN'T FINISH: Baseline imports failed` (the headline symptom)**

- `bootstrap-cache/install-main.ps1` was cached ~6 weeks earlier and never refreshed (log: `using cached install.ps1 for main`).
- That old script pinned the venv to **Python 3.11**, while `pyproject.toml` gates *every* core dependency behind `; python_version >= '3.14'` (changed on main 2026-09-27).
- Result: `uv pip install -e ".[all]"` against the 3.11 venv **silently skipped every gated dependency** (`openai`, `python-dotenv`, `rich`, `prompt_toolkit`, …) — 61 packages installed, zero core deps — and only then did the baseline import gate fail:
  `Baseline imports failed in <install-dir>\venv (dotenv/openai/rich/prompt_toolkit)`
- **Retrying could never work**: the stale cache was never invalidated, so every retry replayed the identical failure. I had to delete the cached script by hand to force a fresh download.

**2. Missing `uv.lock` disabled the verified tier, and the suggested recovery command cannot work**

- With `uv.lock` absent from the worktree the installer logs `uv.lock not found -- falling back to PyPI resolve (no hash verification)` and drops to plain `uv pip install`.
- The failure dialog then suggests: `Recover with: … uv sync --extra all --locked` — which **cannot succeed without the lockfile** (and would fail on the 3.11 venv anyway, since the lock only covers `python_version >= '3.14'`). Recovery hints should be validated before they are shown.

**3. `raw.githubusercontent.com` fetch has no mirror/proxy fallback**

- The bootstrap's own script download failed twice: `resolve install script failed: GET https://raw.githubusercontent.com/… (os error 10054, connection reset)`.
- Notably, `git fetch` inside the same installer already succeeds through a mirror (configured via `insteadOf`), but the HTTP downloader has no equivalent fallback. My workaround was copying `scripts/install.ps1` from a local clone into `bootstrap-cache/install-main.ps1` by hand.

**4. pm tool unpack: transient `WinError 5` kills the whole `python-deps` stage**

- Installing the managed CPython distribution failed moving `tree\python\DLLs -> tree\DLLs` with `[WinError 5] Access is denied` — a transient lock on freshly extracted DLLs (almost certainly antivirus scanning; the same rename succeeded manually minutes later, and the stage succeeded on the next full run).
- The internal retry gave up after 2 attempts within ~15 s and failed the entire stage. Backoff should be longer/exponential for rename-after-extract, and the message should distinguish "file in use" from a real ACL problem.

**5. `products` stage: Electron + electron-builder toolsets download straight from GitHub Releases**

- `electron-v40.10.2-win32-x64.zip` (138 MB) stalled at 4–33% across attempts, then `TypeError: fetch failed`; `icons-bundle.tar.gz`, 7zip, and the winCodeSign kit (ATS dlib, .NET runtime, Windows SDK, rcedit) all come from the same host.
- Setting the standard ecosystem mirrors completed **all** downloads in ~3 minutes:
  - `ELECTRON_MIRROR=https://npmmirror.com/mirrors/electron/`
  - `ELECTRON_BUILDER_BINARIES_MIRROR=https://npmmirror.com/mirrors/electron-builder-binaries/`

### Sanitized log excerpts

```
[bootstrap] using cached install.ps1 for main
-> uv.lock not found -- falling back to PyPI resolve (no hash verification)
{"ok":false,"stage":"dependencies","reason":"Baseline imports failed in <install-dir>\\venv (dotenv/openai/rich/prompt_toolkit). … Recover with: … uv sync --extra all --locked"}
[bootstrap] downloading install.ps1 for mutable ref main from GitHub
ERROR resolve install script failed: GET https://raw.githubusercontent.com/… (os error 10054)
[X] python: install failed: [WinError 5] … '…\.staging-xxx\tree\python\DLLs' -> '…\tree\DLLs' … retry, or run `hermes pm doctor`
downloading label=electron progress=6%   (repeated, then)   TypeError: fetch failed
```

## Proposed Solution

1. **Invalidate the cached install script** (TTL / conditional request / pin it to the fetched commit) so an old script can never pair with a newer `pyproject.toml`. At minimum, warn when the cached script is older than N days.
2. **Fail fast on version mismatch**: before installing, verify the venv interpreter satisfies the dependency markers of the checked-out `pyproject.toml` (e.g. core deps are 3.14-gated while the venv is 3.11) and print an actionable error — instead of "Baseline imports failed" after a green-looking install.
3. **Mirror-aware downloads with automatic fallback**: honor `ELECTRON_MIRROR` / `ELECTRON_BUILDER_BINARIES_MIRROR` (already standard in the Electron ecosystem) and add an equivalent fallback for `raw.githubusercontent.com` requests (mirror list or a `HERMES_DOWNLOAD_MIRROR` knob), mirroring what git already does via `insteadOf`. Consider auto-falling back to a known mirror after repeated 10054/10060 connection resets.
4. **Validate recovery hints**: never suggest `uv sync --locked` when `uv.lock` is absent — suggest restoring it first (`git checkout -- uv.lock`) or omit the `--locked` tier explanation.
5. **Exponential backoff** for `WinError 5` / sharing-violation retries right after extraction; don't fail the whole stage after two quick attempts.
6. **Document the mirror environment variables** in the Windows install/troubleshooting docs.

I'm happy to re-test any fix on this network environment.

## Alternatives Considered

- **Require users to configure a system proxy**: unrealistic for most users in this region; the installer already works around this for git, so the HTTP paths should be consistent.
- **Ship a full offline bundle**: large maintenance burden; automatic mirror fallback is smaller and benefits every restricted-network user (not just China).

## Feature Type

- Performance / reliability

## Scope

- Medium (few files, < 300 lines)

items.title: Fresh first-use grammar download can fail its 60-second deadline on a working slow connection
items.body:
## Fresh consumer acceptance

A clean Python 3.14.4 venv installed treesitter-chunker 5.2.0 and tree-sitter-language-pack 1.20.0 with `--no-cache-dir --require-hashes --only-binary=:all:` from the dotfiles lock. Import and pip check succeeded, but first real Python chunking failed because the language-pack grammar-bundle downloader exceeded its global 60-second deadline. This occurred during simultaneous tooling downloads; a slow but functioning public connection is sufficient to trigger it.

```python
import chunker
chunks = chunker.chunk_text("def consumer_smoke():\n    return 42\n", language="python")
assert chunks
```

The Linux x86_64 grammar bundle is 22,571,517 bytes. After a separate fresh official download (no cache reuse) and SHA-256 verification against the official manifest, putting that verified content-addressed bundle into the private language-pack cache made the same smoke pass with one chunk. No package code or consumer lock was altered.

Official artifact: https://github.com/xberg-io/tree-sitter-language-pack/releases/download/v1.20.0/parsers-linux-x86_64.tar.zst

Expected SHA-256: `f72a6cc06efdc70785ebd283ecfae23e650f12211887349898594c78757d0f5b`.

Please account for slow first-use grammar acquisition: document/offer a bounded verified prewarm route or propagate configurable download deadlines and actionable recovery. A parser execution deadline is distinct from this artifact-download deadline (Consiliency/treesitter-chunker#143 / Consiliency/treesitter-chunker#207).

Consumer evidence and current lock refresh: Consiliency/dotfiles#52.

items.title: [resources] 11-tablegpt-agent: the packaged IPython profile dir is root-owned, so the pybox kernel dies at start under `USER agent` and every code execution returns "Execution timed out"
items.body:
**Component:** `resources/agents/11-tablegpt-agent/Dockerfile`, `bindings/bridge.py`
**Checked at:** ABB `main` 06afd79f (= official/main). The runs used ABB 2464526d / 62210ee8; the unit is unchanged since then (only `ground_truth/.gitkeep` was added).

## Summary

TableGPT runs the analysis code it writes in a local IPython kernel (`pybox`), started with `--profile-dir` set to the profile that `tablegpt` ships, `/usr/local/share/ipykernel/profile/tablegpt`. `pip install` runs as root, so that directory is `root:root 755`. The container then runs as `agent`.

At startup, IPython has to create `security/` (and `log/`, `pid/`) inside the profile dir. It can't:

```text
File ".../IPython/core/profiledir.py", line 141, in check_security_dir
    self._mkdir(self.security_dir, 0o40700)
File ".../IPython/core/profiledir.py", line 106, in _mkdir
    os.mkdir(path, mode)
PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/usr/local/share/ipykernel/profile/tablegpt/security'
```

The kernel dies before it replies to `kernel_info`. TableGPT's tool doesn't surface that: it returns `Execution timed out. Please try again.` (`agent/src/tablegpt/tools.py:97,147`) for every call. So the model keeps retrying, and the Agent either gives up or ends in `GraphRecursionError`.

The build-time check (`Dockerfile:13`) imports `DEFAULT_TABLEGPT_IPYKERNEL_PROFILE_DIR` and `AsyncLocalPyBoxManager` but never starts a kernel, and it runs as root anyway.

## Where (06afd79f)

- `11-tablegpt-agent/Dockerfile:11-14`: `pip install "./agent[local]" …` as root, then `useradd … agent`; `:18` `USER agent`. Nothing chowns the profile dir or points IPython elsewhere.
- `11-tablegpt-agent/bindings/bridge.py:29`: `AsyncLocalPyBoxManager(profile_dir=DEFAULT_TABLEGPT_IPYKERNEL_PROFILE_DIR)`.

## Evidence

- 25 of 36 archived tablegpt-agent runs (campaign 2026-10-04 … 10-07) have the `PermissionError` above in `diagnostics.json` (kernel stderr).
- Examples. Each has the `PermissionError` once, at kernel start, and `Execution timed out` in the tool results after that. All were sent to the Judge:

| Run | Steps | Execution | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `01297e19d8b44dac86c9b5c3142a68b1` | 4 | failed | `insufficient_evidence` |
| `033768a6bc5544b088605167bcba7203` | 10 | succeeded | `insufficient_evidence` |
| `4aae79661d73406e8d70c4f3916c0d5a` | 10 | failed | `insufficient_evidence` |
| `9bb120e04f214cb38e81d656f660fdb8` | 4 | succeeded | `issue` |
| `002c61882a0c41468fa4f588c0b3bc2d` | 3 | succeeded | `issue` |
| `5ed3e94c601e406bbbd56adefb4bf641` | 6 | succeeded | `issue` |

## How to check

No network and no credentials are needed, only the image ABB builds for this unit:

```bash
docker run --rm --network none --entrypoint sh <tablegpt image> -c \
  'id; ls -ld /usr/local/share/ipykernel/profile/tablegpt; python -c "from IPython.core.profiledir import ProfileDir; from tablegpt import DEFAULT_TABLEGPT_IPYKERNEL_PROFILE_DIR as d; ProfileDir.find_profile_dir(d)"'
# uid=…(agent) … drwxr-xr-x root root … /usr/local/share/ipykernel/profile/tablegpt
# PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/usr/local/share/ipykernel/profile/tablegpt/security'
```

End to end, start a kernel the way `bridge.py` does and run `print(6*7)` (a 10-line script that calls `AsyncLocalPyBoxManager(profile_dir=…).start()` and then `box.run(code="print(6*7)")`, run with `-w /tmp`):

```text
RuntimeError: Kernel died before replying to kernel_info
TimeoutError: Timeout waiting for kernel ready.
```

## Suggested fix

Make the profile dir writable by the runtime user, and fail the build if that can't be done. This is what our batch overlay appends:

```dockerfile
USER root
RUN d=/usr/local/share/ipykernel/profile/tablegpt && test -d $d/startup && mkdir -p $d/security $d/log $d/pid \
    && chown -R agent:agent $d && chmod -R a+rwX $d
USER agent
```

(Upstream it can be folded into the existing `RUN` after `useradd`. Copying the profile into a per-Case writable directory and passing that to `AsyncLocalPyBoxManager` would also work, and it keeps `/usr/local` read-only.)

The same two checks on the image built with this addition:

```text
drwxrwxrwx agent agent … /usr/local/share/ipykernel/profile/tablegpt (security/ log/ pid/ startup/)
profile ok /usr/local/share/ipykernel/profile/tablegpt/security
RESULT data=[{'text/plain': '42\n'}] error=None
```

Our overlay also sets `OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1`, so the kernel's numeric libraries stay inside the 128-pid limit (#158). That is separate from this bug.

I don't yet have a completed Case run on the fixed image. The tablegpt batches we ran after the change failed on the model side (gateway `credit insufficient balance`). They show no `PermissionError`, but they also never reached code execution. So far the fix is verified by the kernel probe above.

items.title: agent-dispatch: install.ps1 update can hang/wedge on a live venv slot (same class as #2174); orphaned uv.exe can block all future attempts
items.body:
## What

Observed on a busy multi-plugin Windows machine running `agent-dispatch`'s review-loop supervisors (2 `supervised-lane` registrations + 2 `emitter` registrations actively running out of `versions/0.11.6-dev1`):

1. **`install.ps1 update` can hang indefinitely (eventually exits 124)** when the active venv slot is in use by live supervisor/coordinator processes. Root cause: `Invoke-Update` calls `Install-Runtime` (which runs `uv pip install --reinstall-package agent-dispatch ...` **in place** into the currently-active `versions/<version>` slot) *before* `Retire-SupervisorProcesses` is reached (that only happens later, inside `Install-SupervisorTask`). If any supervisor/coordinator process from that exact slot is still alive -- the normal steady state on a machine actually running the review loop -- the reinstall contends with open file handles on the running interpreter and can hang.
   - This is the same bug class already found and fixed for `agent-worktrees` in #2174 ("Deploy-Package reinstalls into the active version slot on every update, colliding with live daemon file locks"). That fix doesn't appear to have been ported to `agent-dispatch`'s own `install.ps1` (same script lineage/pattern, same `Install-Runtime`/`uv pip install --reinstall-package` shape).
   - Workaround that reliably works: run `install.ps1 stop` first (which *does* correctly retire supervisors + coordinator before anything else), then `install.ps1 update`, then it picks the services back up automatically. But an operator calling plain `update` (the documented/expected path, and what `agent-worktrees update --force`'s plugin-payload-update step does under the hood) hits the hang with no indication why.

2. **A killed/aborted `install.ps1 update` can leave an orphaned `uv.exe pip install ...` child process running indefinitely**, still holding a handle on the target venv's `python.exe`. This silently wedges *every subsequent* update attempt (including a correctly-ordered `stop` + `update`) until a human manually finds and kills the zombie PID -- there's no detection/cleanup of a stale `uv.exe` from a prior failed attempt before starting a new one. Confirmed via `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process` showing a `uv.exe --reinstall-package agent-dispatch ...` process whose `CreationDate` was ~11 hours older than the current attempt, still alive and still blocking.

3. **Separately** (different lock, same symptom class): `copilot plugin update agent-dispatch` fails outright with `Failed to install plugin: The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process. (os error 32)` whenever *any other* Copilot CLI session on the same machine currently has the plugin loaded. This is at least surfaced with a clear error (unlike 1/2 above) -- flagging for awareness since it's the same underlying "payload directory in active use" class as #2385 (agent-ssh's `dtssh-companion.ps1`), just for `agent-dispatch`. No action requested here beyond cross-linking; a shared multi-session machine makes this a real, recurring friction point for picking up any plugin update.

## Where
- `plugins/agent-dispatch/scripts/install.ps1`
  - `Invoke-Update` (ordering: `Install-Runtime` before supervisor/coordinator retirement)
  - `Install-Runtime` / its `uv pip install --reinstall-package agent-dispatch ...` call (in-place reinstall into the live slot, no pre-check for in-use processes, no stale-uv-process cleanup before starting)

## Suggested fix
Port the fix pattern from #2174 (slot-completeness/hash check via `versioned_runtime.py`'s `is_complete`, called before `Deploy-Package`-equivalent `Install-Runtime`, plus retiring supervisors/coordinator *before* any in-place reinstall rather than after) to `agent-dispatch`'s `install.ps1`. Additionally, before starting a new `uv pip install --reinstall-package` run, detect and reap/warn about an already-running `uv.exe` process targeting the same venv rather than silently queuing behind it forever.

## Repro
On a machine with `agent-dispatch` supervisors actively running (registered `supervised-lane`/`emitter` entries with live child processes under `versions/<version>/Scripts/python.exe`):
```powershell
install.ps1 update   # hangs, eventually times out (exit 124)
```
vs. the working order:
```powershell
install.ps1 stop     # correctly retires supervisors + coordinator first
install.ps1 update   # succeeds cleanly
install.ps1 start    # (not even needed -- Invoke-Update already restarts both)
```

items.title: security(admission): classify accepted pip constraint option abbreviations
items.body:
Refs #128 / canonical Agent Artifact Admission PR #129.

## Verified finding

Current test-only head `e2007957cb5b1409d32df9753d2d3d037781068a` exposes a second pip `optparse` prefix-semantic gap in the reviewed constraint authority. Wardnet rejects exact `--constraint` and `--build-constraint`, but pip accepts unambiguous long-option prefixes before Wardnet hands argv to the installer.

Pinned upstream evidence is `pypa/pip@2b28a816d043826f2ba10ff1d22ec3d94d2ed7c5`:

- pip imports and uses Python `optparse` for CLI options;
- `cmdoptions.py` defines `--constraint` and `--config-settings`; those are the only `--con...` options in the pinned shared option surface, so `--con` is ambiguous while `--cons` uniquely selects `--constraint`;
- `cmdoptions.py` defines `--build-constraint`; `--build-c` uniquely selects that build-constraint authority in the pinned option surface.

Both attached-value forms keep the external constraint document out of positional-artifact counting while pip still consumes it as constraint authority.

## Hosted semantic RED

Exact test-only head `e2007957cb5b1409d32df9753d2d3d037781068a` adds hostile direct-pip cases `--cons=https://x.invalid/c.txt` and `--build-c=https://x.invalid/b.txt` to the existing constraint contract. CI `34606386616`, rust job `103285721803`, used a real `ubuntu-24.04` runner; checkout, pinned Rust toolchain and formatting all passed, then `Test` failed and Clippy was skipped. Security Scan `34606386684` and SAST Semgrep `34606386523` are already SUCCESS on the same exact head. This is semantic RED, not checkout/runner/format noise.

## Minimum causal GREEN

For direct `pip install` / `pip3 install` only, classify the pinned parser's accepted unambiguous prefixes for the two already-forbidden authorities:

- `--constraint`: from shortest accepted `--cons` through the full canonical spelling;
- `--build-constraint`: from shortest accepted `--build-c` through the full canonical spelling.

Cover attached and separate-value forms. Do not apply pip abbreviation semantics to `uv`, do not guess shorter ambiguous prefixes, and do not broaden into fetching/parsing constraints, build isolation, package resolution, runtime environment discovery, quarantine execution, or EgressWeave transport authorization.

Exact-head GREEN requires formatting, locked workspace tests, strict Clippy, Fuzz, Security Scan, SAST and then-live review/thread evidence on one unchanged head. Keep this issue open until #129 or a verified complete successor carrying all RED/GREEN/test/doc/evidence delta reaches protected `main`.

## TRACEABILITY

- Python Packaging Authority. (2026). *pip CLI option definitions*, commit `2b28a816d043826f2ba10ff1d22ec3d94d2ed7c5`, `src/pip/_internal/cli/cmdoptions.py`.
- Python Software Foundation. (2026). *optparse — Parser for command line options*. Python documentation; long options may be abbreviated when the prefix is unambiguous.
- National Institute of Standards and Technology. (2022). *Secure Software Development Framework (SSDF) Version 1.1* (NIST SP 800-218).
- MITRE. (2025). *CWE-15: External Control of System or Configuration Setting*.

items.body:
# `hermes update` fails with "The lockfile at `uv.lock` needs to be updated" whenever a pip mirror is configured

## Summary

With a package mirror configured in pip's config (`index-url` in `pip.conf` / `pip.ini`), the
package-manager update path cannot build its own runtime, so `hermes update` fails outright:

```
→ Handing off to the new updater (package manager) for the rest of this update...
Preparing the isolated Hermes runtime…
  → Installing Python dependencies…
  ✗ Installing Python dependencies failed; last 3 lines of output:
      Resolved 5 packages in 297ms
      error: The lockfile at `uv.lock` needs to be updated, but `--locked` was provided.
      hint: To update the lockfile, run `uv lock`.
Source update preparation failed: venv: uv sync exited 1: Resolved 5 packages in 297ms
error: The lockfile at `uv.lock` needs to be updated, but `--locked` was provided.
hint: To update the lockfile, run `uv lock`. — retry, or run `hermes pm doctor`
```

The git side of the update succeeds (commits are fetched and checked out); it dies at
`pm`'s runtime bootstrap. Receipt records `"outcome": "failed"`, `"exit_code": 1`,
`"stop_reason": "sys.exit(1)"`, and `hermes update` never completes.

This reproduces on both Linux (Ubuntu) and Windows 11 installs of the same version, and it
blocks every update for anyone behind a pip mirror (e.g. common mainland-China setups) until
the mirror is disabled.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.21.5 (git install), `main` @ `78999579c8` / `73a9dc598b`
- PM-pinned toolchain: Python 3.14.7, uv 0.12.3
- Linux: Ubuntu, `~/.pip/pip.conf` with `index-url = https://mirrors.aliyun.com/pypi/simple/`
- Windows 11: `C:\Users\<user>\pip\pip.ini` with `index-url = http://mirrors.aliyun.com/pypi/simple/`

## Root cause

1. `pm/index_config.py::bridged_index_settings()` deliberately forwards the user's pip index
   to uv — for a pip-only mirror, pip's `index-url` is translated into `UV_INDEX_URL`
   (`pm/index_config.py` docstring: "a pip-only mirror … is bridged to `UV_INDEX_URL` unless uv
   already has an index of its own").
2. `pm/runtime_stage.py:40` builds the isolated PM runtime with `locked=True`, so uv is invoked as
   `uv sync --locked --all-packages … --no-install-project --no-install-package hermes-pm-runtime --no-config`.
3. `pm/environment.py::PythonEnvironment._run()` passes the bridged `UV_INDEX_URL` down to that
   uv process.
4. `pm/uv.lock` records `source = { registry = "https://pypi.org/simple" }` for every package.
   With **any** explicit index configured, uv considers the lock's resolution to no longer match
   the configured index and refuses to proceed under `--locked`.

The comparison is literal: `UV_INDEX_URL=https://pypi.org/simple` — exactly the spelling the
lock records — is accepted, while `https://pypi.org/simple/` (same URL, trailing slash) fails.
So the trigger is not the mirror's identity but that the bridged index URL is not byte-identical
to the lock's recorded registry.
`pm/runtime_stage.py` hardcodes `locked=True`, so there is no user-facing way to opt into
`--frozen`.

## Minimal reproduction

Using the locked PM project exactly as the updater does (temp copy of `pm/pyproject.toml` +
`pm/uv.lock`, PM-pinned uv/python):

```bash
D=$(mktemp -d); cp pm/pyproject.toml pm/uv.lock "$D/"; cd "$D"

# fails
UV_INDEX_URL=https://mirrors.aliyun.com/pypi/simple/ \
  uv sync --locked --all-packages --python <pm-python> --compile-bytecode \
  --no-default-groups --no-install-project --no-install-package hermes-pm-runtime --no-config
# → error: The lockfile at `uv.lock` needs to be updated, but `--locked` was provided.  (exit 1)

# no index configured → succeeds, installs the 4 runtime packages (exit 0)
uv sync --locked --all-packages --python <pm-python> --compile-bytecode \
  --no-default-groups --no-install-project --no-install-package hermes-pm-runtime --no-config

# mirror configured but --frozen instead of --locked → succeeds (exit 0)
UV_INDEX_URL=https://mirrors.aliyun.com/pypi/simple/ \
  uv sync --frozen --all-packages --python <pm-python> \
  --no-default-groups --no-install-project --no-install-package hermes-pm-runtime --no-config
```

| index configured | flag | result |
|---|---|---|
| none | `--locked` | ✅ installs 4 packages |
| `https://pypi.org/simple` (byte-identical to the lock's registry) | `--locked` | ✅ installs 4 packages |
| `https://pypi.org/simple/` (trailing slash) | `--locked` | ❌ lockfile needs to be updated |
| `https://mirrors.aliyun.com/pypi/simple/` | `--locked` | ❌ same |
| `https://pypi.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/simple` | `--locked` | ❌ same |
| `https://mirrors.aliyun.com/pypi/simple/` | `--frozen` | ✅ installs 4 packages |

Reproduced on current `main` (`73a9dc598b`).

## Impact

- Any install whose pip config points at a mirror cannot update at all — every automatic
  desktop-app update and every manual `hermes update` dies at the same step.
- The only working workaround is to make the process blind to pip's config
  (`PIP_CONFIG_FILE=/dev/null` on POSIX, `PIP_CONFIG_FILE=nul` on Windows — note the comparison
  is against `os.devnull`, so it must be lowercase), which forces downloads to come straight
  from `files.pythonhosted.org`. Measured from the same host:

| route | throughput |
|---|---|
| pypi/files.pythonhosted.org direct | 0.08 MB/s |
| same via a local proxy | 0.07 MB/s |
| Aliyun mirror | 10.6 MB/s |
| Tsinghua mirror | 10.5 MB/s |

  Index latency: pypi.org 0.86 s vs Tsinghua 0.04 s vs Aliyun 0.18 s. So the workaround trades
  a hard failure for roughly a 100× slower download — impractical for a 4000-commit catch-up
  (a ~600 MB dependency set), which is exactly when people run the updater.
- The escape hatch (`PIP_CONFIG_FILE`) is not documented anywhere and is only discoverable by
  reading `pm/index_config.py`.

## Suggested fixes (any one would unblock this)

1. **Don't verify the index under a bridge that PM itself injected.** Either sync the PM runtime
   with `--frozen` (the lock is still fully honoured and hashes still verified — see the table
   above) or pass `--no-sources`, so a user-configured index cannot invalidate a lock whose
   packages are already pinned by hash.
2. **Bridge as a default index the lock can tolerate** (`UV_DEFAULT_INDEX` semantics) rather than
   overriding the index identity, if uv's matching rules allow it.
3. **Surface a supported knob** to disable index bridging for a run (e.g. a config key or
   `hermes pm --no-mirror`), instead of requiring `PIP_CONFIG_FILE=<devnull>`.
4. **Regression test**: `tests/pm/test_index_bridging.py` covers the bridge in isolation, but not
   the combination "bridge active + `--locked` sync", which is the path every updater takes.

## Workaround (for anyone hitting this today)

```bash
# POSIX
PIP_CONFIG_FILE=/dev/null hermes update

# Windows PowerShell — lowercase nul, and the value only lasts for this window
$env:PIP_CONFIG_FILE="nul"; hermes update
```

Removing/commenting `index-url` in `pip.conf` / `pip.ini` also works, at the cost of all pip
traffic going to pypi.org.

## Related

- #79434 — same error string, different mechanism (relative `exclude-newer` span in the root lock).
- #123171 — `hermes pm repair fails when lockfiles are out of sync` (mentions the same error on
  Windows/Python 3.14.7; I could not open that page while writing this, so the overlap is unverified).

items.title: Telegram adapter silently degrades to Any stubs on ImportError, masking real failure
items.body:
**File:** `plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py:236-276`

`except ImportError: TELEGRAM_AVAILABLE = False` sets every Telegram class (`Application`, `Bot`, `HTTPXRequest`, `TypeHandler`, etc.) to `typing.Any` as a fallback stub — but never logs *why* the import failed.

If `telegram` (python-telegram-bot) fails to import for a transient reason (e.g. a race between a gateway/service restart and a pip dependency sync still writing the package's `dist-info`/module files), the code doesn't fail fast. Instead it proceeds all the way to `Application.builder()...build()` / `HTTPXRequest(...)`, which then try to instantiate `Any`, producing:

```
ERROR hermes_plugins.telegram_platform.adapter: [Telegram] Failed to connect to Telegram: Any cannot be instantiated
```

This message gives zero indication of the real root cause (a swallowed `ImportError`), making it very hard to diagnose — especially since `TELEGRAM_AVAILABLE` is only checked later with a *different*, more helpful message ("python-telegram-bot not installed. Run: pip install python-telegram-bot") that never gets logged in this path because the import technically "succeeded" (bound everything to `Any`) rather than raising.

**Suggested fix:** log the original exception in the `except ImportError:` block, e.g.:

```python
except ImportError:
    logger.exception("[Telegram] python-telegram-bot import failed; platform will be unavailable")
    TELEGRAM_AVAILABLE = False
    ...
```

That would surface the actual traceback instead of the misleading downstream `Any cannot be instantiated` TypeError.

🤖 Filed via Claude Code after triaging a stale-checkout/gateway-restart incident where this exact race occurred.

- Alpine / musllinux containers
- Windows x86_64
- less common Python runtimes or platforms

```text
OS / distro:
CPU architecture:
Python version:
pip or uv version:
Install command:
Full error log:
Output of: python -m pip debug --verbose | head -80
Output of: python -c "import platform, sys; print(sys.version); print(platform.platform()); print(platform.machine())"
```

Known implementation direction:

- ship Rust inside the default `litellm` platform wheels
- expose the native module under the `litellm` package, e.g. `litellm._rust_bridge`
- use PyO3 + maturin for binary wheel builds

- make Docker source builds install Rust only in the builder stage; runtime images should not need Rust

items.title: `Agent(retries=N)` re-executes tool calls that already succeeded
items.body:
When `retries` is enabled, a run that fails *after* a tool has completed
successfully is replayed from the beginning, re-executing that tool. For a
non-idempotent tool — a payment, a message, an order — this produces duplicate
irreversible effects.

The retry loop wraps the entire run and catches bare `Exception`, so it cannot
distinguish a failure that occurred before any effect from one that occurred
after.

This is not about ambiguous or timed-out tool calls. The tool in the
reproduction below **succeeds and returns normally**; agno holds its result and
discards it when the subsequent model call fails.

## Reproduction

agno 3.0.10, openai SDK 3.16.2. A local OpenAI-compatible endpoint alternates:
odd request returns a `charge_card` tool call, even request returns HTTP 500.

```python
agent = Agent(
    model=OpenAILike(id="scripted", api_key="not-needed",
                     base_url=LOCAL_URL, max_retries=0),  # SDK retry off
    tools=[charge_card],   # returns normally; appends to a durable ledger
    retries=2,
)
agent.run("charge the card")
```

`max_retries=0` on the model disables the OpenAI SDK's own HTTP retry, so every
repeat is attributable to agno's run loop alone.

### Observed

```
[model] call #1 -> tool_calls(charge_card)
  [tool] EFFECT COMMITTED #1
[model] call #2 -> HTTP 500
WARNING Attempt 1/3 failed. Retrying in 1s...: upstream failure

[model] call #3 -> tool_calls(charge_card)
  [tool] EFFECT COMMITTED #2
[model] call #4 -> HTTP 500
WARNING Attempt 2/3 failed. Retrying in 1s...: upstream failure

[model] call #5 -> tool_calls(charge_card)
  [tool] EFFECT COMMITTED #3
[model] call #6 -> HTTP 500
ERROR   Error in Agent run: upstream failure

agent runs issued by the caller : 1
successful tool executions      : 3
```

### Expected

A tool call that completed successfully should not be executed again because a
later step failed. At minimum, a run containing completed non-idempotent tool
calls should not be replayed silently.

## Where it happens

`agno/agent/_run.py`:

- `426` — `num_attempts = agent.retries + 1`
- `427` — `for attempt in range(num_attempts):`, the body being the whole run:
  session read, model calls, tool execution
- `724` — `except Exception as e:` with no classification
- `732` — logs `Attempt n/N failed. Retrying in Ds...` and continues

Nothing records which tools already executed, and completed tool results are not
reused on replay.

## Suggested changes

Roughly in order of value to cost:

1. **Reuse completed tool results on replay.** agno already persists run
   messages, so the tool results from the failed attempt are available. Resuming
   from them — replaying the model call but not the tool — would fix the common
   case without changing the retry API.

   I probed the live retry branch to check this rather than assume it. At the
   moment the retry decision is made:

   ```
   run_response.tools = None
   run_messages       = 3 messages, including
       role=tool content='charged 100.00 for op-f7-repro-0001'
   ```

   So the successful tool result is in hand when agno decides to replay and
   discard it. This is the same structure as a durable-execution event history,
   minus the decision to consult it.

2. **Do not replay a run in which a tool already executed**, unless the tool is
   known idempotent. Safer and simpler than (1) if resumption is awkward, at the
   cost of some retry coverage.

   **Tested.** With a guard reading the `role="tool"` messages above, the same
   reproduction gives **1 execution instead of 3**, and logs *"Attempt 1/3
   failed after 1 tool call(s) already completed. Not retrying: replaying the
   run would repeat them, and whether their external effects occurred is
   unknown."*

   Worth noting for whoever implements it: the obvious version, checking
   `run_response.tools`, does **not** work — that field is `None` at the retry
   point and the guard silently never fires. I made that mistake first.

   Patch and measurements attached. It covers the sync branch only; the async
   twin near line 1264 needs the same treatment.

3. **Consume the MCP annotations agno already emits.** agno marks its own
   published tools with `readOnlyHint` / `destructiveHint` / `idempotentHint`
   (`agno/os/mcp.py:112-113`, `:2278`). Reading the same annotations on the
   consuming side would identify exactly the tools that must not be replayed,
   and the vocabulary is already standardised by MCP.

4. **Document the hazard on `retries`.** Even without a code change, the
   parameter's documentation could note that enabling it may repeat completed
   tool calls, so it is unsuitable for agents with non-idempotent tools.

## Note on the default

`retries` defaults to `0`, so this is opt-in. Worth saying why it still seems
worth reporting: the failure mode is invisible during testing, because with a
healthy model endpoint the retry loop never executes. It activates when the
provider is degraded — which is also when partial runs are most likely.

## Context

items.title: zava-learning: Container Apps fail to start when tenant policy forces Key Vault publicNetworkAccess=Disabled
items.body:
**Summary**
Deploying labs/zava-learning into a subscription governed by a tenant-level policy that enforces Key Vault private networking causes 8 of 10 Container Apps to fail provisioning. The apps cannot resolve the pg-password secret reference because there is no network path to the vault.

**Environment**
Lab: labs/zava-learning
Region: southcentralus (also reproduced in centralus)
Subscription type: MCAPS-sponsored
azd 1.34.1
What happens
infra/modules/keyvault.bicep line 42 sets publicNetworkAccess: 'Enabled', but the deployed vault comes back Disabled. An explicit az keyvault update --public-network-access Enabled returns HTTP 200 and the value silently reverts — the signature of a modify/deny policy assigned above the subscription.

Since the template creates no private endpoint for the vault, nothing can reach it. Container Apps that reference the secret fail:

ContainerAppOperationError: Failed to provision revision for container app 'quiz-perf'.
Field 'configuration.secrets' is invalid: Invalid value: "pg-password":
Unable to get value using Managed identity .../id-zava-*** for secret pg-password.
Failed (8): quiz-nsg, quiz-perf, quiz-app, quiz-query, quiz-secret, gradebook-api, quiz-pool, quiz-appgw Succeeded (2): course-api, assessment-api — neither references pg-password

RBAC is correct: the user-assigned identity holds Key Vault Secrets User on the vault. This is purely a network-path problem.

**Suggested fixes**
Deploy a private endpoint + private DNS zone for the vault when publicNetworkAccess is unavailable — this matches the policy posture most enterprise and MCAPS subscriptions enforce, and better reflects a production reference architecture.
Alternatively, add a parameter (e.g. useKeyVaultPrivateEndpoint) so deployers can opt in.
At minimum, document the prerequisite in README.md, since the failure surfaces late — after ~10 minutes of successful provisioning — and the error message doesn't point at the vault's network configuration.

**Separate, smaller finding**
infra/modules/vm.bicep hardcodes Standard_D2as_v6, which reports NotAvailableForSubscription in centralus, eastus2, and westus3 on this subscription. Standard_D2as_v7 is available, has the same 2 vCPU / 8 GB shape, and supports the required NVMe disk controller. Worth parameterising the VM size, or moving to v7.

labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

labels.description: Web dashboard / control panel UI (dashboard/, landing)

items.body:
## Symptom

`hermes update` pulls code, rebuilds, restarts gateways — then exits **1** and the Desktop app surfaces "Update didn't finish / Backend update failed", even though the code swap actually succeeded and the version advanced.

Observed on macOS (Mini, Intel), update to v0.21.4 (2026.9.21) / upstream 2332a643.

Receipt (`~/.hermes/logs/update_receipts/latest.json`):
```json
{ "exit_code": 1,
  "stop_reason": "TypeError: _find_stale_dashboard_pids() got an unexpected keyword argument 'scope_home'" }
```

## Root cause

Mixed old/new modules during the code swap: the long-running updater process had already imported `hermes_cli.main_dashboard` **before** the swap (old signature, no `scope_home`), then the post-swap path called it with the new kwarg.

Current HEAD (both correct, so this is a mid-update module-skew problem, not a permanent signature bug):
- `hermes_cli/main_dashboard.py:21` — `def _find_stale_dashboard_pids(*, exclude_pids=None, scope_home: str | None = None)`
- `hermes_cli/dashboard_procs.py:608` — `_dash._find_stale_dashboard_pids(exclude_pids=exclude or None, scope_home=scope_home)`

## Impact

- The update is effectively complete but reported as failed; the Desktop app shows a failure modal ("Try again" / "Not now") and users cannot tell whether to retry.
- Side effect: gateways *were* restarted via launchd (exit 143), but the dashboard/serve restart entries were logged as failed (`✗ serve [default] pid … — planned mechanism: respawn-argv`), and the desktop app build was left stale behind the runtime.

## Suggested fix

Resolve the restart helpers through the module at call time (re-import / `importlib.reload` on the swapped modules) or re-exec the post-swap phase in a **fresh** process so no pre-swap modules are live — the same class of skew already called out by the existing warning: "⚠ A previous hermes update pulled new code but did not restart running gateways. Gateways may still be serving pre-update modules (mixed sys.modules)."

Repro: run `hermes update` while an updater process already has `main_dashboard` imported and the incoming tree changes that function's signature.

items.title: agent-worktrees: transient ModuleNotFoundError from a self-update venv-swap race (distinct from #3999)
items.body:
## Symptom

`agent-worktrees` transiently failed with `No module named agent_worktrees` immediately after a fresh self-update deployed a new version (`deploy-manifest.json` recorded `deployed_at` for the new version a moment before the failing invocation). Re-running the exact same command seconds later, and directly invoking the same venv's `python.exe -c "import agent_worktrees"`, both succeeded cleanly with no other change -- the interpreter, `sys.path`, and package contents were all intact and correct once inspected.

## Root cause (hypothesis)

A live-cutover race in the self-update mechanism: the deploy pointer/manifest appears to get marked "done" fractionally before the new version's venv `site-packages` payload finishes being written/settled on disk, so any foreground CLI invocation landing in that narrow window sees an incomplete/inconsistent package tree and raises `ModuleNotFoundError`.

## How this differs from #3999

#3999 (`ImportError: MARKETPLACE_MANIFEST_RELS`) was a **stale/incompatible runtime slot** -- an old, no-longer-matching venv left in place. This is a **live in-flight cutover race** against a version that ends up perfectly fine once the race window closes -- a different failure shape, same race family (atomic-publish / TOCTOU) the `full-harness-startup-reliability` effort has been hardening in Round 8/9 for the binstub stamp marker and first-time-install paths.

## Why this wasn't caught by existing tests

Per that effort's own Round 8 finding, prior regression tests invoke `init.ps1` (or equivalent) directly from a repo checkout, which never matches the self-stage guard's real `.copilot/installed-plugins/` marketplace path -- "a real marketplace install is the only place this bug actually bites." A race gated on genuine marketplace self-update timing is structurally invisible to that test methodology. There is also no `drain`/`undrain`-style gate protecting a plain foreground `agent-worktrees <verb>` CLI invocation from a concurrent runtime-slot cutover; that primitive only guards `agent-bridge`'s own live sessions today.

## Suggested fix direction

Apply the same atomic-publish discipline already applied to the binstub stamp marker (Round 8/9) to the versioned runtime-slot venv swap itself: only flip `current-version`/`deploy-manifest.json` to point at the new slot after the entire venv payload (including `site-packages`) has been fully written and verified importable, not merely copied.

## Cross-references

- `ThomasMichon/copilot-extensions#3999` (related but distinct stale-slot symptom)
- Effort: `efforts/active/full-harness-startup-reliability` (this repo, aperture-labs-owned worktree) -- same race family as Round 8/9's atomic-publish findings

items.title: Fix: Packaging metadata does not include runtime dependencies from `requirements.txt`

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

items.body:
# Packaging metadata does not include runtime dependencies from `requirements.txt`

## Summary

`setup.py` already reads dependencies from `requirements.txt`, but the parsed dependencies are never passed to `setup()` through `install_requires`. As a result, the generated package metadata does not declare Ianvs' runtime dependencies, which can lead to missing dependency errors after installation.

---

## What happened

Installing Ianvs as a Python package (for example, using `pip install .` or `pip install -e .`) does not automatically install all runtime dependencies required by the project.

Although `setup.py` parses `requirements.txt` via `_infos.basic_dependencies`, the value is never passed to the `install_requires` argument of `setup()`. Consequently, the package metadata does not list Ianvs' runtime dependencies.

This can cause the installed CLI to fail immediately with import errors such as:

```text
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'colorlog'
```

---

## What you expected to happen

Installing Ianvs as a Python package should automatically install all runtime dependencies declared in `requirements.txt`, allowing the `ianvs` CLI to run without additional manual package installation.

---

## How to reproduce

1. Clone the repository.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/kubeedge/ianvs.git
cd ianvs
```

2. Install Ianvs as a package.

```bash
pip install -e .
```

(or)

```bash
pip install .
```

3. Run the CLI.

```bash
ianvs
```

4. Observe that startup may fail with an error similar to:

```text
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'colorlog'
```

---

## Root cause

`setup.py` already contains logic to read dependencies from `requirements.txt`.

For example:

```python
@property
def basic_dependencies(self):
    return self._read_requirements(self._requirements)
```

However, these dependencies are never passed into the package metadata via:

```python
install_requires=...
```

As a result:

- `requirements.txt` exists.
- `setup.py` successfully parses it.
- The parsed dependencies are discarded.
- The generated package metadata does not advertise the runtime requirements.

---

## Additional observations

During inspection, two runtime dependencies were also found to be required by the source code:

- `colorlog`
  - imported by `core/common/log.py`
- `PyYAML`
  - provides the `yaml` module imported by `core/common/utils.py`

If these packages are absent from the declared runtime dependencies, users may encounter import errors even after successfully installing Ianvs.

---

## Suggested fix

Use the already existing dependency parser by passing the parsed requirements into `setup()`:

```python
install_requires=_infos.basic_dependencies,
```

Also ensure that `requirements.txt` contains all runtime dependencies required by the project (including packages such as `colorlog` and `PyYAML` if they are intended runtime requirements).

---

## Impact

This issue affects package installations performed through standard Python packaging workflows, including:

- `pip install .`
- `pip install -e .`
- installation from source
- any future distribution built from the package metadata

Without proper dependency metadata, installations may succeed while the application fails immediately at runtime because required packages were never installed.

---

## Environment

- OS: macOS
- Python: 3.x
- Installation method: `pip install -e .`

items.title: Parallel installs can fail to resolve setuptools due to a SeparateBodyFileCache race

labels.name: status/external-issue
labels.description: Issue is caused by external project (platform, dep, etc)

items.body:
### Description

We are hitting intermittent setuptools resolution failures during parallel source-package installs with Poetry 2.4.1 in CI. I also reproduced the underlying empty-index failure with **Poetry 2.4.3**, the latest release at the time of reporting, and **CacheControl 0.14.4**.

The failing CI install was preparing `argparse 1.2.1` and `bravado-core 6.1.1`. The package-index request succeeded, but Poetry reported:

```text
Because -root- depends on setuptools (>=40.8.0) which doesn't match any versions, version solving failed.
Cannot resolve build-system.requires for bravado-core.
Package setuptools (84.0.0) not found.
```

The local reproducer demonstrates a cache race consistent with this symptom: `SeparateBodyFileCache` publishes metadata before the separate body file exists. A concurrent Poetry repository lookup can interpret the incomplete entry as an empty package index, either on a fresh-cache hit or during HTTP 304 revalidation. The exact interleaving in the original CI job was not captured.

Expected behavior: concurrent lookups should return the available package links, wait for a complete entry, or treat an incomplete entry as a cache miss.

Related upstream work:

- https://github.com/psf/cachecontrol/issues/324 — non-atomic separate-body cache reads/writes.
- https://github.com/psf/cachecontrol/pull/465 — paired read/write locking; its exact commit passes the focused reproduction below.
- https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/pull/10816 — switched Poetry from `FileCache` to `SeparateBodyFileCache` to support large responses.

This report tracks the impact on Poetry and provides reproduction evidence for evaluating the upstream fix or a Poetry-side mitigation.

### Reproduction

The [standalone script](https://github.com/igormishsky/cachecontrol/blob/3af1c3c1e03425793d67a7d0a4799b7f4ed01607/scripts/reproduce_poetry_cache_race.py) uses a real localhost HTTP server, Poetry's `LegacyRepository`, the native CacheControl adapter/controller, and the actual HTML parser. It adds synchronization around existing calls to force the writer to pause before body publication. It does not mock package lists or parser results.

Requirements: `uv`, Git for the optional fixed control, and Python 3.11 (which uv can provision).

```sh
curl -fsSL \
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/igormishsky/cachecontrol/3af1c3c1e03425793d67a7d0a4799b7f4ed01607/scripts/reproduce_poetry_cache_race.py \
  -o reproduce_poetry_cache_race.py

uv run --no-project --python 3.11 \
  --with 'poetry==2.4.3' --with 'cachecontrol[filecache]==0.14.4' \
  python reproduce_poetry_cache_race.py \
  --expect broken --iterations 5 --output baseline.json
```

`--expect broken` exits successfully only when the failure is reproduced as expected. Each run uses new temporary cache directories, so it does not depend on a previously corrupt cache, Artifactory, or a restored GitHub Actions cache.

There are four schedules, repeated five times: threads/processes sharing a cache, each with fresh reads and HTTP 200/304 revalidation. The server sends an ETag and `Cache-Control: max-age=60`, with no `Content-Length` or `Vary` header. One reader sees zero links although the response contains `setuptools-84.0.0-py3-none-any.whl`.

#### Results

| Poetry | CacheControl | Empty-index failures |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| 2.4.1 | Released 0.14.4 | 20/20 |
| 2.4.3 | Released 0.14.4 | 20/20 |
| 2.4.1 | Original #465 commit `7df32057203eb379f51149da204bddd3d3447bdc` | 0/20 |

The original upstream commit was tested without the additional changes in my fork. To run that control:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/trail-of-forks/cachecontrol.git cachecontrol-465
git -C cachecontrol-465 checkout 7df32057203eb379f51149da204bddd3d3447bdc

uv run --no-project --python 3.11 \
  --with 'poetry==2.4.1' --with 'cachecontrol[filecache]==0.14.4' \
  python reproduce_poetry_cache_race.py \
  --cache-source ./cachecontrol-465 \
  --expect fixed --iterations 5 --output fixed.json
```

Poetry remains unmodified and caching stays enabled. With that commit the reader waits for body publication, and both workers find the expected link. Subsequent warm-cache lookups make zero additional HTTP requests. The script prints loaded source paths because the checkout still reports the distribution version as 0.14.4.

These are deterministic HTTP/cache/index-parsing tests, not complete application installs or measurements of natural failure frequency. No wheel is downloaded or executed. Separate fault-injection tests still expose interrupted-write and concurrent 304-update gaps in the original #465 commit; the passing result above is limited to the reproduced read-during-publication failure.

### Workarounds

`poetry --no-cache install ...` bypasses the affected HTTP cache. A separate focused test of Poetry 2.4.1's CLI cache-bypass path passed 5/5 overlapping repository lookups. This has not been validated as a full application-build fix in this report. Clearing the cache alone does not prevent recurrence: every failing reproduction starts with a fresh temporary cache.

### Poetry Installation Method

Other: uv-managed isolated environments with pinned Poetry and CacheControl versions.

### Operating System

Local reproduction: macOS 15.7.7, arm64, Python 3.11.5.
Observed CI symptoms: Amazon Linux 2023 on arm64 and amd64, Poetry 2.4.1.

### Poetry Version

```text
Poetry (version 2.4.3)
```

Also tested with Poetry 2.4.1, as shown above.

### Poetry Configuration

The standalone reproducer constructs `Config(use_environment=False)` and overrides only `cache-dir` with a fresh temporary directory and `keyring.enabled` with `false`. It uses a localhost `LegacyRepository`, with no credentials or plugins. The two concurrent workers are explicitly created by the harness.

Relevant defaults, confirmed using an isolated `poetry config --list`:

```text
installer.max-workers = null
installer.no-binary = null
installer.only-binary = null
installer.parallel = true
installer.re-resolve = false
requests.max-retries = 0
solver.lazy-wheel = true
virtualenvs.create = true
virtualenvs.in-project = null
```

### Example pyproject.toml

Not required for the standalone reproduction: it exercises Poetry's repository lookup directly. The original symptom occurs during isolated build-system dependency resolution for source distributions.

### Poetry Runtime Logs

The CI error excerpt is above. The standalone script directly exercises the repository API rather than invoking `poetry install`, and records actual HTTP requests and parsed links in its output JSON.

Selected summary fields from the Poetry 2.4.3 baseline run:

```json
{
  "poetry_version": "2.4.3",
  "cachecontrol_distribution_version": "0.14.4",
  "expectation": "broken",
  "total": 20,
  "empty_indexes": 20,
  "both_workers_succeeded": 0
}
```

The HTTP sequence is `[200]` for a fresh read and `[200, 304]` for revalidation. In each baseline trial the writer finds the wheel link, while the reader returns `[]` before the writer is released. With original #465, both return the wheel link and the reader completes after the writer is released.

items.title: release-failure: v0.17.0 workflow failed
items.body:
**Workflow:** release.yml
**Tag:** v0.17.0
**Run:** https://github.com/pgmnemo/pgmnemo/actions/runs/31779847615
**Triggered by:** psychologistgbi-beep
**Event:** push

One or more jobs in the release workflow failed. Common causes:

- **pre-flight failure** → version mismatch between `pgmnemo.control` / `META.json` / `pgmnemo_mcp/pyproject.toml` / `CHANGELOG.md`. Check the pre-flight job log for the specific assertion.
- **installcheck failure** → `pg_regress` regression diffs uploaded as artifact `regression-diffs` on this run.
- **bench-gate failure** → `benchmarks/gate/v0.17.0.json` missing or invalid.
- **release / PGXN upload failure** → `PGXN_USERNAME` / `PGXN_PASSWORD` secrets unset, or manager.pgxn.org rejected the bundle.
- **publish-mcp / PyPI failure** → OIDC trusted publisher not configured (see pypi.org/manage/account/publishing/), or `PYPI_API_TOKEN` secret invalid.
- **smoke-pypi failure** → `pip install pgmnemo-mcp==0.17.0` succeeded but import broke. Check for empty-wheel regression (#32 class).
- **smoke-pgxn failure** → typically PGXN propagation delay, treated as warning. If it persists >10 min, investigate manually.

### Recovery steps

1. Fix the underlying issue (likely a version mismatch or missing artifact)
2. Delete and recreate the tag: `git tag -d v0.17.0 && git tag -a v0.17.0 -m '...' && git push origin v0.17.0 --force`
3. Re-run will trigger automatically on the new tag push.

items.title: stdio: concurrent sessions log each other out, `pip install .` installs no dependencies, list-write tools can never be authorized (+ a sign-in page bug)
items.body:
**Repo:** ProcessQualitySolutions/qcdatabase_mcp, checked at `75fed7c`

Hi Larry, I found three bugs in the local (stdio) server while using it day to day. The patch at the bottom of this issue fixes all three, with tests. I can send it as a PR if you'd prefer. I've been running the patch locally since 2026-10-02. I also hit a bug in the qcdatabase.ai sign-in page while testing (#4), which needs a fix on the platform side.

Good news first: stdio works. The README banner saying the "stdio tools are broken" (added 2026-07-13) is out of date, and the patch removes it.

---

### 1. Running several sessions at once logs every session out

Each desktop AI session starts its own stdio server, so I usually have two or more running at a time. They all share `store.json`, and two things combine badly:

- `Store` reads the file once in `__init__`. After that, every write dumps the process's whole in-memory copy back to disk (`config.py:65-87`).
- Refresh tokens rotate (`auth.py:301`).

So when process A refreshes, process B is left holding a dead refresh token. When B's access token expires, B refreshes with that dead token and gets a 400. B then runs `clear_token()` (`auth.py:291`), which wipes the token from disk for every session. Separately, any write from B (`set_active_project`, for example) overwrites A's newer token with B's stale copy.

**What users see:** "Your session expired and could not be refreshed. Run 'login' again." for no obvious reason. Also, a new session can start on a project left over from a different session.

**Reproduced:** `tests/test_store_concurrency.py` (in the patch) runs four `Store` instances that refresh at once against a token endpoint that rotates refresh tokens. On `main` that produces two "session expired" errors, plus a `PermissionError(13)` on Windows from two processes calling `os.replace` on the file at the same time. With the patch, the token is refreshed exactly once and every session gets the new token.

**Fix in the patch:**
- `Store` reads from disk on every read, and each write re-reads the file under a lock and changes only its own key. The lock is a cross-process file lock (`msvcrt` on Windows, `fcntl` elsewhere) and is re-entrant within one process.
- `refresh()` runs entirely inside that lock. It re-reads the token first, and if another process has already refreshed, it uses that token instead of spending the old refresh token.
- On a 401, the client passes the token that was rejected (`refresh(..., rejected=...)`). The token is cleared only if it is still that same token (`clear_token(if_access_token=...)`).
- The active project is now kept per process. A new session still starts on the last project chosen, but one session switching projects no longer changes the project of another running session. I think this is the safer behavior, since writes go to whatever project is active.

### 2. `pip install .` (the README install step) gives a server that can't start

`[project.dependencies]` is empty, and the real dependencies sit in the `runtime` extra (`pyproject.toml:27`). I understand why: the comment explains the managed-build `uv sync` problem. But the README still says `pip install .` and `pip install -e .`, and so does every `scripts/run-*` launcher. In a clean virtual environment:

```
pip install .
python -c "import qcdatabase_mcp.server"
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'httpx'
```

**Fix in the patch:** the README and all four launcher scripts now install `".[runtime]"`. The `pyproject.toml` arrangement is unchanged.

### 3. `create/update/delete_list_item` are exposed but `lists:write` is never requested

`DEFAULT_SCOPES` includes `lists:read` but not `lists:write` (`auth.py:51`, which says lists are "read-only by design"). The three list-write tools are still exposed, so every call returns 403. Logging in again doesn't help: `_register_client` reuses the cached registration, and its scope is the client's permanent ceiling.

(One more small thing I noticed: the list-items API accepted an item with empty `data` even though that list's schema marks four fields `required`.)

### 4. Platform bug: the sign-in page drops the OAuth authorize parameters

This one is in qcdatabase.ai, not this repo, but it breaks `login` for anyone who isn't already signed in to the site.

`/oauth/authorize/?response_type=code&client_id=...&redirect_uri=...&scope=...&state=...&code_challenge=...` sends a signed-out browser to `/login/?next=...`. The 302's `Location` encodes `next` correctly. But the login page writes `next` into the form's `action` **unencoded**:

```
action="/login/?next=/oauth/authorize/?response_type=code&client_id=...&redirect_uri=..."
```

So after signing in, `next` keeps only `/oauth/authorize/?response_type=code`, and everything after the first `&` is lost. The consent page then shows "An application wants to access your account", "No specific permissions requested", and empty hidden fields for `client_id`, `redirect_uri`, `scope`, `state`, and `code_challenge`. Clicking **Authorize** does nothing. I reproduced this today; once already signed in, the same URL renders the consent page correctly.

**Fix:** URL-encode `next` when the login template builds the form action (e.g. `{{ next|urlencode }}`), or carry `next` in a hidden input instead of the query string.

- **Errors aren't flagged as errors.** `_safe` returns errors as normal text starting "Error: ..." with `isError` unset, so an agent running a batch can count a rejected call as a success. Raising `ToolError` would set the flag.
